title: Правда о Париже и засада в шкафу  (The Truth About Paris and Hiding in the Closet)

segments.t: Inside Vika's apartment, Max hides in the closet while Vika firmly tells Igor that she does not love him, only for Igor to kiss her just as Max peers out. Back in the kitchen, Chef Barinov furiously reveals to his cooks that 'Valdemar Barani' is actually Volodya Baranov, his former sous-chef in Paris.
Игорь, а что ты хочешь от меня услышать?
Почему мы не можем быть вместе?
Ну, потому что я не люблю тебя.
Этой причины достаточно?
До сих пор сохнешь по своему поваренку.
А это тебя уже точно не касается.
Я не понял?
У вас было или не было?
Шеф, чего вы не сказали, что знаете Барани?
А я и не знаю Барани.
А это кто?
Моим су-шефом в Париже.
Теперь всем понятно, почему между нами такая любовь?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Игорь, а что ты хочешь от меня услышать?

'Igor, what do you want to hear from me?' By wondering what Lyova wants to hear from him, Barinov presses Lyova for a straight answer. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Почему мы не можем быть вместе?
'Why can we not be together?' Asking why they not be together can cuts straight through the tension between Lyova and Barinov.
Ну, потому что я не люблю тебя.

'Well, because I do not love you.' Adding that because he does not love Lyova fills in the missing piece for Lyova. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Этой причины достаточно?

'Is that reason enough?' Here checking whether that reason enough shows Lyova looking for the real truth. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
До сих пор сохнешь по своему поваренку.
'You are still pining for your little cook.' Since Lyova is still pining for Lyova's little cook, Barinov does not waste words on excuses.
А это тебя уже точно не касается.

'That is definitely none of your business anymore.' Mentioning that that is definitely none of Barinov's business anymore moves the talk in a new direction. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Я не понял?
'Wait, I did not get that?' When Barinov asks if he did not get, Lyova has to answer fast. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
У вас было или не было?
'Did something happen between you two or not?' Here asking whether something happen between Barinov two or not shows Lyova looking for the real truth.
Шеф, чего вы не сказали, что знаете Барани?

'Chef, why did you not tell us that you know Barani?' By wondering why Lyova not tell them that Lyova knows Barani, Barinov presses Lyova for a straight answer. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
А я и не знаю Барани.
'I do not know any Barani.' Lyova mentions that he does not know any Barani so Barinov sees what is at stake.
А это кто?
'Then who is that?' Over the shift and the apartment, Barinov presses Lyova for a straight answer.
Моим су-шефом в Париже.
'As my sous-chef in Paris.' With the kitchen and moment in play, Lyova keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Теперь всем понятно, почему между нами такая любовь?

'Now does everyone understand why there is such love between us?' By asking whether everyone understand why there is such love between them, Barinov presses Lyova for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.

Теперь всем понятно, почему между нами такая любовь?

That wraps up this scene as vika rejects Igor's advances while Max hides inside her apartment, and back at the restaurant Chef Barinov bitterly tells the cooks how his former sous-chef Volodya Baranov betrayed him in Paris. See you next time!
Хорошего дня!
